summary: The CA-root inventory rewrite is correct and independently re-derived — nine real copies, five image-baked, the two symlinks rightly excluded — and the digest half of the pin rule checks out. But the pin sentence's appended gloss defines an estate-wide first-party tag norm that four code sites falsify, in the one phase whose whole outcome is that sentence being true. Two advisory findings ride along: the inventory's next bullet names a copy KubeCoder deleted on 2026-09-03, and P7's enumeration of the runbook's count sentences misses one.

findings.summary: decisions.md:599's new gloss says first-party builds publish :<build> and :latest and consumers reference :latest; matrix images publish neither and four consumers pin.

decisions.md:167, the same inventory's next bullet, still names /work/KubeCoder/controller/homelab-root.crt, deleted in KubeCoder 7e78405f — a wrong rotation procedure the phase's one-directional sweep could not catch.
P7's enumeration of the runbook's count sentences omits step-ca-root-rotation.md:132 ("The seven paths are duplicates by convention"), two lines above the md5sum block that grows to ten.
